what: Pick the next exercise demo films by what members actually do: first every exercise in the beginner ready programs and the most-logged lifts, then the rest
why: Only 2 of the roughly 400 library exercises have a demo film today, so almost every member opens an exercise and sees no film; the film queue is one a day, so its order decides what members get first
impact_why: A new member on Full Body Basics would see a film on every exercise of their first weeks instead of on two side exercises
my_view: My view: do it; it changes only the order of the queue the film tool already works through, no app change. The beginner programs hold a few dozen distinct exercises, about a month of the one-a-day pipeline.

what: Give the "lose fat" goal its own shape: a 10-minute cardio finish (treadmill, cycle or skipping) at the end of each plan-builder workout, and one ready "Fat loss, 3 days" gym program
why: Fat loss is one of the four goals a member can pick, but the builder leaves all cardio out and treats fat loss like muscle, and no ready program is written for it; weight loss is a very common reason people join an Indian gym
impact_why: A large group of new members picks this goal and today gets the same plan as someone building muscle
my_view: My view: do it; treadmill and cycle logging already exists, so it is one extra slot on fat-loss plans plus one program of data. Keep the lifting the same; the cardio is the only change, and say so on the plan.

what: Add a "Classic 5-day split" ready program (chest, back, shoulders, arms, legs: one muscle group a day), and a 2-day full-body program for busy weeks
why: The ready programs are only 3, 4 or 6 days a week, while the plan builder already accepts 2 to 6 days; the one-muscle-a-day split is what many Indian gym trainers write on the board, and a member who trains that way finds nothing familiar in the list
impact_why: Members who already follow a 5-day split can follow it in the app with Target lines from day one instead of building every routine by hand
my_view: My view: do it; it is data only (the program shape and the test that checks every exercise already exist). Say in its summary that training each muscle twice a week suits most people better, so we meet members where they are without calling it the best split.

what: Let the plan builder ask one optional extra question, "Anything to focus on?" (legs and glutes, upper body, arms, none), and add one more exercise for that area to each workout
why: The builder asks goal, level, equipment, days, time and sore areas but never what the member most wants to change; a glutes and legs focus is a common ask from women members, and Fitbod lets members set muscle priorities (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live)
impact_why: Makes the built plan feel made for the member, which is the reason to use the builder instead of a ready program
my_view: My view: worth doing after the fat-loss shape; keep it to one answer and one extra slot so the time per workout still fits, with "none" as the default.

what: Put the member's goal, level, training days a week and equipment (home, dumbbells, full gym) at the top of the "Ask your own AI" text, and ask the AI to answer in Hindi when the app is in Hindi or Hinglish
why: The text gives the AI only exercises and sets, so its advice can tell a home trainer to use a cable machine or a fat-loss member to bulk; the question is always in English even when the member reads Hindi
impact_why: Better answers from the AI make the feature worth repeating, but few members use it today
my_view: My view: do it; none of these four facts can identify the member or divide back to body weight, so the privacy promise holds. Keep name, phone and weight out as now.

what: Celebrate a new strength level on the finish screen ("Bench press: now Intermediate"), the day a best lift moves the member up a level
why: The level sits quietly under the chart on each exercise page, so a member who moves up a level usually never notices; a level change is rare and real, the kind of moment that keeps people coming back
impact_why: A rare, earned milestone at the end of a workout gives the member a reason to share and to return
my_view: My view: do it; show the level word only (no body weight, no ratio), the same privacy rule as the exercise page, and at most one level line per workout.

what: Let a gym owner attach a real reward to a badge in the panel (for example "50 workouts: a free shaker at the desk"), show it on the member's locked badge, and list who earned it on the desk screen
why: Badges live only on the member's phone; the code already notes a gym prize as a later idea. Gyms judge MettleUp on members still training on day 30, and a prize at 10 or 50 workouts is a cheap reason for a member to keep logging and for the owner to keep paying
impact_why: Ties the free app to the gym's own retention, the number the owner pays for
my_view: My view: worth building once more gyms are live; it needs the server to know which badges a member earned, so start with the workout-count badges (10 and 50), which typing made-up weights cannot fake.

what: Warn the member before an easy week starts, on the Today card ("Next week is an easy week: half the sets"), and let them move it from there
why: The easy week is explained only once it has begun, behind the i on the Target line and the Today card; a member planning a hard week finds out at the gym
impact_why: Fewer members skip the easy week by surprise, and the plan feels planned
my_view: My view: do it if cheap; the next-easy-week rule already exists, so it is one line on the Today card in the last days of the week before.
